clue.text: Cancels a lease, sadly holding first of regular events caused by shops closing down

definitions.text: events caused by shops closing down

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters wrap around the single letter taken from regular
sadly suggests the words are knocked out of shape, so the letters of Cancels a lease are rearranged
first of picks only the opening letter of the word regular

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper glumly ends a lease, and regular closing-down events follow as the shop shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges CANCELS A LEASE; 'holding' puts R ('first of regular') inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops that are shutting hold sales to clear their stock, which is what a clearance sale is.

clue.text: International agency wanting some nun escorts

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An international body is looking for a few nuns to act as chaperones.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'wanting' into the definition; it is only a link word joining the agency to its wordplay, and 'International agency' alone names the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization is a specialised agency of the UN.

clue.text: Film star entertaining a clergyman

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the film star's name takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent-film comedian

explanation.surface: A movie star plays host to a member of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like it describes the star's job, but it means holding A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a hospital, school or regiment.

clue.text: The point of love seats, essentially

wordplay.reading: E S E, the middle letters of loveseats

parts.note: the middle three letters of the run loveseats are E, S, E, the abbreviation of this compass point; 'essentially' asks for the heart of the words

explanation.surface: A wry remark on what a sofa for two is really for.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'loVESEats' – its middle letters E S E – is the abbreviation, which you write out in full in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the sixteen named directions on a compass rose, halfway between east and southeast.

clue.text: Class containing one who's especially talented?

definitions.text: Class containing one who's especially talented?

indicators.note: containing means the word for class holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind in biological classification
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A school class with one gifted pupil in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a genus with one brilliant individual in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of exceptional intellect or creative gift is called a genius.

clue.text: Event curtailed tennis game, with police brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the police letters are placed inside the rearranged ones
game can mean lame or crooked, so the shortened word is bent into a new order
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the word tennis loses its final letter

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A tennis match cut short, and the police called in: quite an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' docks the last letter, and 'game' (lame, crooked) rearranges what is left to INENT. 'brought in' puts the detectives inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an occurrence or happening, especially one that is notable.

clue.text: Result of mob rule? Former Taoiseach lost a wife

parts.note: Jack Lynch was Ireland's Taoiseach (prime minister) in the 1960s and 1970s
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports league tables

explanation.surface: An Irish former prime minister suffers a loss: his wife has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Taoiseach is the Irish prime minister; Jack Lynch held the office twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Summary punishment by a mob without a trial is the consequence when crowds take justice into their own hands.

clue.text: Italian in no great hurry, locking up a shed?

indicators.note: locking up means the slow tempo word holds the letter a shut inside it

parts.note: lento is the Italian musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: A leisurely Italian takes his time padlocking a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian in no great hurry' looks like a person, but it is the musical tempo marking LENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or outbuilding propped against a wall; the question mark admits it is one kind.

clue.text: Sailor briefly having a break, being between two ships

definitions.text: Sailor briefly having a break, being between two ships

parts.words: Sailor briefly having a break, being between two ships
parts.note: the short form of this rank is O S, and those two letters sit either side of the gap in 'two ships'

explanation.surface: A sailor on shore leave, between postings on two vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the abbreviation OS, which straddles the break between 'twO' and 'Ships'; write the rank out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the lowest rating of seaman in the Royal Navy and merchant navy, abbreviated OS.

clue.text: Website creator's skill becoming evident as GP changed Iris's treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked on and handled into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A web designer's talent shows when a family doctor alters a patient's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' looks like the anagram signal but is itself fodder; 'treatment' rearranges GP, CHANGED and IRIS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying out images and type for a site is visual communication work, a core part of building websites.

clue.text: Storyteller regularly made us soup

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter from the words made us soup

explanation.surface: A storyteller was in the habit of cooking soup for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like 'often', but it takes alternate letters: mAdE uS sOuP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist is credited with tales such as The Tortoise and the Hare.

clue.text: Playing dirtier ultimately, if one is in a blue funk

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about, so dirtier and the two end letters are rearranged
ultimately picks the last letter of each of the words if and one

explanation.surface: A player fears that playing dirty will get them caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives F and E, the ends of 'if' and 'one'; 'Playing' rearranges them with DIRTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue funk is a state of extreme fear or panic, so someone in one is scared stiff.

clue.text: A very dishonourable chap breaking into orchard's heading repeatedly for a kind of pear

indicators.note: breaking into means the cad's letters go between the pair of picked letters
repeatedly says the picked letter is used twice over
heading picks the first letter of orchard's

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A scoundrel breaks into an orchard repeatedly to steal pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading repeatedly' gives O twice; 'breaking into' puts CAD between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is often called an alligator pear or avocado pear for its pear-like shape.

clue.text: Back door Bill Clinton finally needed

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, i.e. a poster

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Clinton

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton needs a back way in, perhaps to avoid the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Clinton' reads as the former president, but 'Bill' is a printed notice and only Clinton's last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear or side gate, especially in a castle or fortification.

clue.text: One carrying red box around, in case one's needed in church

parts.note: a cabinet is a case or cupboard for storing things

indicators.note: needed in means the numeral goes inside the word for church

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone carries a red box about in case it is needed at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: British government ministers carry papers in red despatch boxes, as the Chancellor famously shows on Budget day.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior UK government members are issued red boxes for their state papers, which they carry everywhere.

clue.text: Attractive bloke on vacation before Advent

indicators.note: before places the emptied bloke ahead of the next part
on vacation means emptied, so the word bloke keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: advent means an arrival or coming

explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptied out: BlokE leaves BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that flatters you is said to be becoming, meaning attractive or suitable.

clue.text: Pinter production described by papers as daring

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the papers letters enclose the rearrangement

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: a production of a play reworks it on stage, so the letters of Pinter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper critics call a new staging of a Harold Pinter play bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges the playwright's name into NTREP; 'described by' means drawn round, as in geometry, so the papers enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrepid person is fearless and adventurous, ready to take bold risks.

clue.text: Second Oscar award for Welsh comedian

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A second Academy Award goes to a comic from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Secombe was a Welsh comedian and singer, one of the Goons on BBC radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Harry Secombe was a much-loved entertainer from Swansea, famous from The Goon Show.

clue.text: Animal, maybe male, raised by Paddy

parts.note: raised means up
a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet

explanation.surface: An animal, perhaps a male one, has been brought up by a man called Paddy.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal is the wild drummer in The Muppet Show band; 'Paddy' is a temper tantrum, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal is one of Jim Henson's puppet characters, the frenzied drummer of the Electric Mayhem band.

clue.text: Criminal used to needing uniform inside, once obedient

indicators.note: inside means the letter for uniform is placed within the rearranged letters
criminal suggests wrongdoing, so the letters of used to are bent into a new order

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An ex-con, used to wearing prison uniform, was once well-behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges USED TO into DTEOUS, and 'inside' puts U within. 'once' marks the answer as old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiful and submissive is an old-fashioned sense now rarely heard, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Intercourse initiator "on top", perhaps leading to another possible choice

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be in another order, so they are rearranged
initiator means the starting letter of Intercourse

explanation.surface: A risqué suggestion about who takes the lead in bed, opening up other possibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I and ON TOP together.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of several alternatives open to you, a choice you may take.

clue.text: Those sharing secrets of a politician in primarily left-leaning columns

indicators.note: in means the politician goes inside the outer letters

parts.note: posts are upright columns or pillars
A plus MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: In spycraft, chalk marks on street lighting standards signal that a dead drop is loaded, so they pass on secret messages.

clue.text: Especially wide, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning particularly or unusually
in cricket a wide is a run awarded for a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, one kind of run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: Especially broad, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of reach; the run it gives is one of the bonus runs added to the total.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes, leg byes, wides and no-balls are the cricket term for runs not credited to a batter.

clue.text: Low-down on paper doll?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's inside story on a toy doll.

clue.text: Current viral complaint contracted in an Indian city, in general

indicators.note: in means the current and the shortened illness are placed inside the city

parts.note: Agra is the city in India home to the Taj Mahal

parts.note: the common cold is a viral illness
